claims.statement: EU guidance permits food no longer marketable for human consumption, including unsold bread and broken biscuits, to enter animal feed where it is safe and all feed rules are met.
Feed-chain operators face registration or approval, hygiene, HACCP, traceability, safety and labelling duties; a digital exchange does not remove those duties.

Packaging contamination prevents direct feed use, and streams containing animal-origin material enter additional animal-by-product rules; eligibility therefore cannot be granted generically to a bakery, brewery or factory.

Poland publishes a register of establishments approved or registered under feed-hygiene rules, making recipient-status checks technically possible but not guaranteeing that a listed operator will accept a particular stream.
Poland already has IUNGO sourcing food-sector products and selling specified feed materials, while Trotec is building a former-food processing factory in Przasnysz.
Direct incumbents bundle containers, weighing, registration, processing, technical integration, compliance advice and logistics, so a thin matching layer has no evidenced advantage by itself.
No reviewed direct incumbent page publishes a comparable generator subscription or transaction take rate; willingness to pay 500-1500 PLN per stream monthly remains unknown.

contrary_evidence: IUNGO has operated in Poland since 2004 and already sources food-sector products, processes them and sells specified feed materials.
Trotec is constructing a Polish factory and offers an integrated processing, logistics, sensor, data and compliance service rather than a software-only exchange.
FeedValid similarly supplies containers, transport, weighing and registration, indicating that operational execution is part of the incumbent value proposition.
EU food-use hierarchy prioritises prevention and human redistribution before feed where food remains suitable for people.
A successful introduction can be disintermediated when generator and processor contract directly.

economics.acquisition_route: Validate one corridor with one registered processor and three to five generators whose streams the processor pre-accepts conditionally; use the public Polish register and industry associations for a finite prospect list. No paid acquisition should precede evidence that a processor and a generator will use the shared record repeatedly.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Scenario, not forecast: 200 generators at 1000 PLN monthly plus 30 million PLN annual documented GMV at 4% produces 3.6 million PLN annual revenue; at 25% EBITDA and a 6x multiple that is 5.4 million PLN enterprise value before debt. A 5-7 year path requires retaining the subscription and take rate despite direct incumbent relationships; none of those inputs is validated.
economics.founder_time: Initially 15-25 hours weekly for product and bounded customer discovery; classification, HACCP, sampling, transport and recall decisions must remain with qualified operators or advisers. Operations could exceed the founder's limit if the company assumes collection or quality responsibility.
economics.gross_margin_basis: A software and document-orchestration layer could target 65-80% contribution margin only if laboratories, transport, storage, processing and product liability stay contractually with counterparties. Any bundled physical service would materially lower margin and raise capital needs.
economics.payback: Not established. As a mechanical sensitivity, 20 generators at 1000 PLN monthly and 65% contribution would yield 13000 PLN monthly before fixed costs and founder labour, nominally covering 60000 PLN in about five months after that scale is reached; acquisition time and willingness to pay are unknown.
economics.pricing: Test 500-1500 PLN per accepted recurring stream per month and 1-2% of documented offtake, with a no-fee pilot. Direct processors publish contact-based commercial terms rather than comparable software prices, so the original 3-5% take rate has no supporting evidence.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Production and collection recur daily or weekly, but the marketplace can be bypassed after matching. Retention therefore depends on compliance evidence, specification changes, forecasts, recipient-status checks and exception history being valuable every cycle.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A permissioned history of each stream's specifications, accepted recipients, test results, seasonal volume and rejection reasons, provided counterparties continue using the record after the first match.
fingerprint.customer: Polish food manufacturers with recurring, separately stored plant-only former-food or food-production side streams, and registered feed processors seeking specified inputs.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: A bounded regional corridor recruited through the Polish veterinary feed-operator register, food-industry associations, laboratories and existing processors rather than a broad anonymous marketplace.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Stream qualification records, batch and lab evidence, registered-counterparty checks, forecast volumes, forward reservations, exception logs and recall-ready exports; physical handling remains with licensed processors and carriers.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The generator would pay a recurring compliance-record fee after a stream is accepted, with an optional low transaction fee only when a documented offtake is completed; actual payer preference is unvalidated.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A recurring stream loses its human-food outlet and needs a lawful classification, specifications, traceability, eligible recipient and reliable collection or reservation before it can enter the feed chain.

founder_fit: The data, traceability and exception-analysis layer fits the founder's quantitative and AI skills.
A single regional corridor can be tested within the founder's 5-hour daily limit before any wider expansion.
The founder can stay non-public-facing, but qualified feed-law and veterinary support is necessary.
FMCG adjacency is useful only through public knowledge and newly obtained customer data; employer information must not be used.
risks: Feed contamination, packaging residue or misclassification could harm animals or trigger a recall.
Animal-origin ingredients can move a stream into stricter animal-by-product controls.
Transport and drying economics can overwhelm the value of low-price feed materials.
Strong processors can bundle the record-keeping feature or bypass the exchange.
Assuming title, custody or product responsibility would increase regulatory, insurance and capital exposure.
Part-time operation is incompatible with emergency logistics or safety decisions unless those duties remain with qualified partners.

structure.commercial_archetype: Regulated side-stream workflow and forward-offtake network
structure.control_point: The recurring stream authorization record bound to batch evidence and an eligible receiver
structure.critical_dependency: A feed-law-compliant classification and processor commitment for each stream, plus a reason for both parties not to revert to a direct relationship

thesis: A Poland-first compliance and forward-reservation layer can help food manufacturers place recurring, plant-only former-food streams with registered feed operators, but only stream by stream after feed-law classification, safety controls, labelling and eligible-recipient checks. The evidence supports lawful feed use and recurring supply, while direct incumbents already bundle collection, processing, logistics and production data; willingness to pay for a software-only exchange remains unknown.
title: Former-Food-to-Feed Forward Offtake Exchange
uncertainties: How many Polish generators have recurring eligible volumes not already contracted to processors or waste operators.
Which exact plant-only stream classes processors will pre-accept and at what minimum volume, radius and specification.
Whether a generator or processor will pay a recurring software fee after the first match.
Actual laboratory frequency, rejection rate, transport cost, feed-equivalent price and spoilage window by stream.
Whether the platform itself would be treated as a feed business operator or broker under the intended contractual flow.
Whether insurers and counterparties will accept the proposed allocation of contamination, recall and mislabelling liability.
